```{r, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning=FALSE)
# plotly.js from the CDN, so the site's pages don't each copy it
options(plotly.core.plotlyjs = "cdn")
```
#### Basic Histogram

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(50))

fig
```

#### Normalized Histogram

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(50), histnorm = "probability")

fig
```

#### Specify Binning Function

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

x <- c("Apples", "Apples", "Apples", "Organges", "Bananas")
y <- c("5", "10", "3", "10", "5")

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(y = y, x = x, histfunc = "sum") |>
  update_layout(yaxis = go_yaxis(type = "linear"))

fig
```

#### Horizontal Histogram

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(y = rnorm(50))

fig
```

#### Overlaid Histograms

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(500), opacity = 0.6) |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(500) + 1, opacity = 0.6) |>
  update_layout(barmode = "overlay")

fig
```

#### Stacked Histograms

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(500), opacity = 0.6) |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(500) + 1, opacity = 0.6) |>
  update_layout(barmode = "stack")

fig
```

#### Cumulative Histogram

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(
    x = rnorm(50),
    cumulative = go_histogram_cumulative(enabled = TRUE)
  )

fig
```
### Share bins between histograms

In this example both histograms have a compatible bin settings using the `bingroup` attribute (see `go_histogram()`). 
```{r}
library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(100, 5), bingroup = 1) |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(20, 5), bingroup = 1) |>
  update_layout(barmode = "overlay", bargap = 0.1)

fig
```
Note that traces on the same subplot, and with the same `barmode` ("stack", "relative", "group") are forced into the same `bingroup`, however traces with `barmode = "overlay"` and on different axes (of the same axis type) can have compatible bin settings. Histogram and [histogram2d](2d-histogram.html) trace can share the same `bingroup`.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(100, 5)) |>
  add_histogram(x = rnorm(20, 5)) |>
  update_layout(barmode = "stack", bargap = 0.1)

fig
```
### Reference

See `go_histogram()` for more information and chart attribute options!
